sections.overview: Pandalus borealis is a cold-water shrimp of northern Atlantic and Pacific seas, important in several northern fisheries.
sections.identification: Its body is translucent to pinkish and its shell is relatively thin; Pacific Pandalus eous is a distinct, very close relative, not a local form of P. borealis.
sections.habitat: It lives over soft seabeds in cold marine waters, with a broad circumboreal range from the North Atlantic to the North Pacific.
sections.diet: It is an opportunistic omnivore that acts as both predator and scavenger on the seabed.
sections.behavior: Its life history includes sex change: young shrimp mature first as males, with females appearing later; timing varies by region.
sections.reproduction: Eggs are carried by the female, and spawning is seasonal; local timing and reproductive investment vary across its range.
sections.ecology: The close relative P. eous differs taxonomically; in the Gulf of St Lawrence, Pandalus montagui is distinguished by stronger red bands, not treated as a synonym.
sections.conservation: NOAA reports the U.S. northern-shrimp stock as overfished and its fishery closed; that regional finding should not be generalized worldwide.
